# Verify a target fact

Adapters may only rely on facts recorded in `docs/target-facts.md`. Vendor docs change
monthly and memory is not evidence.

## Evidence levels, strongest first
| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| SMOKE | Observed by running the installed tool in a throwaway fixture |
| HELP | Read from the installed tool's `--help` or feature listing |
| DOCS | Stated in vendor documentation (cite the URL); a claim, not proof |
| UNVERIFIED | Neither; do not build on it |

## Steps
1. Record the installed version: `claude --version`, `codex --version`.
2. Prefer a SMOKE test. Build the smallest fixture that shows the behaviour, in a scratch
   directory, with a unique marker string (e.g. `MARKER-SKILL-PROJECT`) so the result is
   unambiguous.
3. Useful probes:
   - Claude: `claude -p "<question>" --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 1` and
     read the `system`/`init` event (`agents`, `skills`, `mcp_servers`, `memory_paths`). It
     costs one short model call.
   - Codex: `codex debug prompt-input "<prompt>"` renders the model-visible input without a
     login or model call.
4. Never write to `~/.claude*`, `~/.codex*` or any account folder to set up a test. If a fact
   needs that, record it as DOCS or UNVERIFIED and say why.
5. Add or update the row in `docs/target-facts.md`: what the spec assumes, what the tool
   does, status and how it was checked. Update the date and version in the header.
6. If the fact changes an adapter's verified version range, update the adapter's
   `verified` field so `alz doctor` warns outside it.

Report the fact, its status and the command that showed it.
